'''Arthur Nobile''' (May 6, 1920 – January 13, 2004) was an American microbiologist.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2023-08-16 |title=NIHF Inductee Arthur Nobile and Prednisone History |url=https://www.invent.org/inductees/arthur-nobile |access-date=2023-08-18 |website=www.invent.org |language=en}}</ref> He is best known for his isolation and reproduction of the [[steroids]] [[prednisone]] and [[prednisolone]].

== Early life ==
Arthur Nobile was born in [[Newark, New Jersey|Newark]], [[New Jersey]] on May 6, 1920. He was a member of the [[United States Army Air Forces|U.S. Army Air Force]] during [[World War II]], where he served in the [[Philippines]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arthur Nobile Obituary (2004) - Newark, NJ - The Star-Ledger |url=https://obits.nj.com/us/obituaries/starledger/name/arthur-nobile-obituary?id=15267652 |access-date=2023-08-18 |website=Legacy.com}}</ref>

== Education ==
Nobile studied at the [[University of Southern California]] and [[Washington State University]] before eventually earning his [[Bachelor of Arts|A.B.]] degree in [[Bacteriology]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1950.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=2000 Awardees |url=http://www.njinvent.org/2000-awardees.html |access-date=2023-08-18 |website=NJ Inventors Hall of Fame 2018 |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
Nobile's work with the steroid drugs prednisone and prednisolone is widely considered one of the largest advances in 20th century medicine.<ref name=":1" />

=== Recognition ===
Nobile was inducted into the [[New Jersey Inventors Hall of Fame]] in 2000 and the [[National Inventors Hall of Fame]] in 2007.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />
